# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 73 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 73 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_073_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 73 concludes Similitude 8. It answers the final rod category (fully green = those who always feared God and never wavered), delivers the universal commission to repentance, and closes with the departure of the shepherd-angel eastward accompanied by the two young men who appeared at the vision's start.

The commission formula in 73:2 is theologically important: "The Lord, being full of compassion (*polysplanchnos*), sent me to grant repentance to all — especially to those who have sinned greatly." The word *polysplanchnos* is a key divine attribute in Hermas — "many-boweled," i.e., deeply compassionate. EMET renders "full of compassion," LOGOS the same, PNEUMA "full of compassion." All agree.

The phrase "called by his great and holy name" (*tō megalō kai hagiō onomati autou epiklēthentes*) refers again to baptism — those on whom the name was invoked. This is the same formula as in 71:1, connecting both ends of the moral spectrum under the same baptismal covenant.

The departure scene is humanizing: the angel is *gelōn* ("laughing") as he departs, and his farewell is *kalōs agōnizou* — "strive well" or "struggle well." EMET has "strive well," LOGOS "strive well," PNEUMA "keep fighting." SOPHIA uses "strive well" as both more literal and dignified.

The awakening and response in 73:4 echo the dream-vision genre throughout Hermas — Hermas wakes, writes, and reflects. The sentence "The Lord has not forgotten me" is a personal theological declaration that grounds the entire prophetic commission in grace.

---

## Similitude 8, Part 4 — The Commission and Departure

**73:1** "Lord," I asked, "those who surrendered green rods and whose rods were found to be green — who are they?" "These," he said, "are those who always feared God and kept his commandments and did not deviate in any way. These are the ones who will dwell in the first tower."

**73:2** After he had completed the exposition of all the rods, he said to me: "Go and tell all people to repent, and they will live for God. For the Lord, being full of compassion, sent me to grant repentance to all — especially to those who have sinned greatly. For the Lord is willing that all who were called by his great and holy name should be saved."

**73:3** After he had finished speaking with me, the two young men who had accompanied him came and carried him away toward the east. As he departed, he was laughing. And he called out to me as he went away: "Strive well."

**73:4** Then I awoke and wrote down everything that had been shown to me. And I was glad, for the things shown to me were great and glorious. When I awoke I said: "The Lord has not forgotten me, but has shown me his grace."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
